0.content: Fontaine Cuisine (also: Fontainian cuisine, Fontainian food, Fontainian gastronomy, Fontaine food): Fontainian cuisine is the refined, elegant, French-style cooking of Fontaine, the nation of justice and theatre. Afternoon tea with desserts is popular among the upper classes, rich dishes like foie gras sit beside humble ones like fish and chips, and Fonta, a bright sweet soda, is the favourite drink. The most famous kitchen is Hotel Debord in the Court of Fontaine, home of the legendary Gateau Debord and, until recently, the chef Escoffier. As in Mondstadt, people there generally dislike spicy food.

1.content:
Daily Life in Fontaine (also: Fontainian daily life, everyday life in Fontaine, Fontainian customs): Everyday life in Fontaine, the Hydro nation of justice, mixes elegant city living with steam-age technology and a love of drama. People ride aquabuses along the waterways, read the newspaper The Steambird, devour mystery novels, go to the theatre as casually as drinking water, and give flowers whose colours carry fixed meanings. Machines called clockwork meka do routine work. Humans share the nation with the Melusines. Below the polished Court of Fontaine, the poorer quarter of Fleuve Cendre is run by the Spina di Rosula, and the law is notoriously fussy.

Practice: Common routines and pastimes: newspaper reading, theatre and cinema, mystery novels, aquabus rides, diving, gifting flowers with set meanings, and following the courts.

2.content: Fontaine Fashion (also: Fontainian fashion, Fontainian clothing, Fontaine clothing, Fontainian dress): Fontainian clothing splits along the line between the city and everywhere else. In the Court of Fontaine people wear formal, decorated outfits, many recognisably Belle Epoque in spirit (cravats, waistcoats, lace blouses, hats), while Fleuve Cendre and areas outside the city favour simpler, practical wear. Most civilian clothes come in many colour schemes, mostly blues, purples, yellows, greens, reds and browns. Many trades have their own uniform, and the best-known name in high fashion is the Inazuman designer Chiori of Chioriya Boutique.

3.content: Fontaine Fashion Week (also: Fashion Week, Fontaine fashion show): Fontaine Fashion Week is a large, recurring social event in Fontaine, held once a year, where fashion designers present new work to the public, sponsors and critics. It gives designers wide exposure and can make or break a name. Chiori of Chioriya Boutique owes her fame to an early Fashion Week yet is not fond of the event as a social occasion.

4.content:
Fontaine Performing Arts (also: Fontainian theatre, Fontainian theater, Fontaine theatre, performing arts of Fontaine): Fontaine is a nation that loves the stage. Theatre, opera, music and magic acts are ordinary life there: per Navia's Character Story, saying you grew up watching the theatre is the same as saying you were raised drinking water. Most shows are held at the Opera Epiclese, which is also the main courthouse. Famous names include the old playwright Coppelius, the Great Magician Lyney and, in recent years, the new film scene.

Practice: - Theatre and opera are part of daily life. Most shows are staged at the Opera Epiclese.
- Music festivals and film festivals are held yearly; the large touring concert is the Iridescence Tour.
- Magic shows are popular, with Lyney as the nation's best-known magician.
- Mystery novels such as "Great Detective Hurlock" and "The Case Files of Miss Orith" are widely read.

5.content:
Religion in Fontaine (also: Fontainian faith, worship of the Hydro Archon, God of Justice worship): Fontaine's faith is devotion to its God of Justice, the Hydro Archon. Egeria, "Mistress of Many Waters", ruled until the Cataclysm and was succeeded by Focalors. For five centuries Fontainians lived under the Prophecy that their sin would one day dissolve them in a great flood. In 4.2 Focalors had herself executed, which destroyed the Hydro Archon's divine throne, and the Hydro Dragon Neuvillette absolved the people. There is now no Hydro Archon.

Practice: Fontainians do not appear to worship through priests or temples. Respect for the God of Justice shows in how seriously the law is taken. The people's belief in justice is felt at every verdict. Fontaine's Statue of the Seven is a monumental figure said to be sculpted in the Hydro Archon's image, and Fontinalia is the festival tied to Egeria.

Scene use: Treat faith in Fontaine as civic and theatrical. A character might invoke "justice" the way others invoke a god, mention Furina's birthday holiday, or speak of the Prophecy as something now over.

6.content:
Fontaine Script (also: Fontainian script, Fontainian writing, Fontaine writing system): The Fontaine Script is the lettering used on signs, posters and shop fronts across Fontaine. It looks like a flowing, cursive version of the common script seen elsewhere in Teyvat, but it mostly spells ordinary English and French words, such as shop names and the label Banque du Nord. Characters just read it as their normal writing.

Practice: Seen on storefronts, café signs and street posters. Typical examples: Bertin's House of Curiosities shows the owner's name, a boutique sign reads couture, and a café sign reads Cafe Lutece.

Scene use: Use it as set dressing: a sign or poster in neat Fontaine lettering, shop names and short French-flavoured labels.

7.content:
Trials as Spectacle in Fontaine (also: Fontaine trials, Fontainian trials, trial by duel, trials at the Opera Epiclese, Fontaine courtroom): In Fontaine a criminal trial is a public show. Cases are heard at the Opera Epiclese, an opera house that doubles as the nation's main courthouse, with an audience watching as attorneys, witnesses and a judge argue it out. Neuvillette presides as Chief Justice (Iudex). Before a trial an accused person may instead demand a duel with an official Champion Duelist to defend their honour: win and they are acquitted, lose and they stand trial. For about five hundred years the final verdict came from a machine, the Oratrice, which stopped working after Furina's trial in 4.2.

Practice: A trial takes place on the stage of the Opera Epiclese with a judge, attorneys, witnesses and the accused before an audience that reacts openly. Until 4.2 the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale delivered the verdict, which the presiding judge had to honour even when he disagreed.

Scene use: Use the trial as a public show. Put characters in the stalls, on the stand or in the gallery, with a lively audience, a formal judge and dramatic turns. Keep the duel as an option for someone who values their honour.

8.content:
Fontinalia Festival (also: Fontinalia, Fontinalia Film Festival, Furina Award, Trial or treat): The Fontinalia Festival is Fontaine's festival remembering the legendary Lochknights, who searched for the Oceanids and welcomed the Hydro Archon Egeria to Fontaine. Traditionally people wore costumes, raised golden cups and went door to door asking for pure water. Furina reshaped it into a carnival in which children collect candy and cry "Trial or treat!". It now also includes the Fontinalia Film Festival.

Practice: Legend says the Lochknights went in search of the Oceanids and in the end welcomed Egeria, the Hydro Archon, to Fontaine. The festival commemorates this: celebrants dress in special costumes, raise golden cups, and visit homes asking for pure water.

key: Iridescence Tour: Lantern Rite Grand Concert
9.content:
Iridescence Tour (also: Iridescence Tour: Lantern Rite Grand Concert): The Iridescence Tour is a music festival that originated in Fontaine. Its organizers, chiefly the travelling musician Dvorak, want to hold it in every nation of Teyvat. It has a poor record on the road: stagings planned for Inazuma and again for the Golden Apple Archipelago were cancelled, leaving the rocker Xinyan stood up twice. It finally happened in Liyue as the Lantern Rite Grand Concert and on Watatsumi Island as Arataki Itto's own rock party. Everything shown of it is limited-time event story.

Practice: It is a touring festival of live music with a changing line-up. The organizers recruit performers, secure a venue and funding, plan rehearsals and a programme, then stage a show. In practice the schedule, funding and local approvals are the weak points.

Scene use: Use it as a hook for music-minded characters: an earnest touring organizer, a call for performers, a rehearsal, or an apology for a cancellation. Keep it small-scale and good-humoured.
